frontier.hypothesis: GATE 1 - the base pseudo in the vJ chassis can be given a byte-free, non-dead, cse1-surviving SECOND SET, which turns off sched.c's birthing_insn_p boost and leaves `la $s0` at the top of the entry block. With that single change vJ should measure at or near 1 (only the peel fold left), since -fno-schedule-insns already proves the rest is target line-for-line.
frontier.mechanism: adjust_priority (sched.c:2584) boosts an insn to max_priority only when n_deaths == 0 AND birthing_insn_p, and birthing_insn_p (sched.c:2504) is exactly `reg_n_sets[i] == 1` for a live SET-of-REG dest. n_deaths is always 0. So any second SET of pseudo 74 disables the sink. The second set must (a) not be dead (DCE removed g1d), (b) not have a constant/constant-equivalent source (cse1 deletes those - s10), (c) not let cse copy-propagate the split away (vK), and (d) resolve to move $s0,$s0 at reload so it costs no byte.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate second-set spellings whose SOURCE is a live REG and whose DEST is genuinely read afterwards: (i) make the base the value the loop reads and the walking pointer the value it writes, i.e. `q = var_s0 + 0x28; var_s0 = q;` inside the loop with nextfile(q) - measure insn count first, it may stay 33 if one of the two copies coalesces; (ii) re-enter the base from the walking pointer at a point where it IS subsequently used, e.g. reuse the base as the nextfile argument on alternate paths; (iii) check whether local_alloc's update_equiv_regs/combine_regs can be made to leave a second set intact by putting the copy in a different basic block from the la. Confirm each with tmp/grind/func_80037A20/s12/allocdbg.sh (reg_n_sets shows up as nrefs/allocno count) and with `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80037A20` reading the .sched dump for the la's priority (a boosted la prints 7f000001, an unboosted one prints 1).

frontier.hypothesis: GATE 2 - on the vJ chassis, defeating the cse1 REG_WAS_0 fold of the peel (`li $s1,1` -> target `addiu $s1,$s1,1`) no longer costs the allocation, so one of the fold-defeat spellings killed in s2/s6/s10 on two-pseudo chassis may now succeed.
frontier.mechanism: The fold is a FIRST-pass cse const-prop of the dominating var_s1 = 0 into var_s1 + 1 (base.i.cse carries a REG_WAS_0 note - s6). Every previous defeat raised Rc 10 -> 11 and lost a 1.25 tie; vJ's margin is 23333 vs 20625 (sched on) and 17500 vs 17368 (sched off), so the pointer keeps $s0 either way. cse1's path is an extended basic block terminated by a CODE_LABEL, so any spelling that puts a surviving label (or a genuinely unknown value) between the zero-init and the peel blocks the propagation.
frontier.next_probe: On chassis_s12_vJ_basewalk.c ONLY, re-run the fold-defeat set that s10 killed on the floor-6 body: do-while(0) around the peel, `var_s1 = var_s1 + 1`, the single-set zero-init local, and additionally read tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c cse_end_of_basic_block to enumerate what terminates the cse path (CODE_LABEL, JUMP_INSN, follow_jumps/skip_blocks limits) and look for an ordinary-C shape that leaves a label between the zero-init and the peel which jump2 later deletes. Measure each with sandbox AND with -fno-schedule-insns (the forensic build isolates gate 2 from gate 1: on the nosched build the peel is the ONLY remaining diff, so a successful fold-defeat there should print a byte-identical function).

frontier.hypothesis: If gates 1 and 2 resist separately, the walking pointer's margin on vJ is large enough (23333 vs 18750) to absorb a FOURTH pseudo, so a further partition may exist that satisfies both gates at once.
frontier.mechanism: The base is allocated last at pri 2500 and still lands in $s0 purely through hard_reg_copy_preferences and the absence of a conflict. That means additional short-lived pointer pseudos joined by no-op copies are essentially free as long as they stay in the same copy-preference class and never conflict with the counter. Each extra pseudo redistributes reg_n_sets and reg_n_refs without changing a byte.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate 3- and 4-pseudo pointer chains (base -> mid -> walking) with the copies placed in different basic blocks so cse cannot propagate them away, and for each measure (a) insn count (must stay 33), (b) ALLOCDBG allocno list and hard regs, (c) whether the la's .sched priority is 1 (unboosted) or 7f000001 (boosted). The winning shape is any chain where the la-carrying pseudo has reg_n_sets >= 2 while the loop-carrying pseudo stays at ~7 refs and a live length of 6-8.
